name: peru
label: Peru
unit: quality-filtered hotspot detections per 0.5° cell and calendar month (UTC)

MODIS.baseline_note: Averages use 2003 onward, when both Terra and Aqua flew; earlier years had one MODIS satellite and read low.
quality_rules: Dropped MODIS confidence below 30 % (FIRMS low class)
Dropped type 1-3 (volcano, other static land source, offshore) where the file reports it
processing: 2026-01-01 to 2026-08-31: FIRMS area API, standard processing

VIIRS.baseline_note: Averages use 2012 onward, the full VIIRS S-NPP record.
quality_rules: Dropped VIIRS low confidence (FIRMS l class)
Dropped type 1-3 (volcano, other static land source, offshore) where the file reports it
processing: 2026-01-01 to 2026-07-31: FIRMS area API, standard processing

harmonization.target: MODIS-equivalent detections: what Terra + Aqua MODIS would likely have reported, estimated from VIIRS S-NPP
harmonization.method: Per calendar month m and 0.5° cell: MODIS ≈ k_m · ((1 + VIIRS)^β_m − 1); β_m is the log-log slope over cell-months with VIIRS detections, k_m matches training totals.
caveats: Scored against MODIS, which is itself a sample of fires, not ground truth.
Terra and Aqua orbits drifted after about 2020 and 2022, so test-year MODIS may read lower for reasons unrelated to fire.
One set of coefficients for the whole country; local landscapes may need their own.

sources: NASA FIRMS area API (2026 onward), clipped to the archive's 0.1° country footprint
limitations: Detections are satellite hotspot pixels, not unique fires or burned area.
MODIS (1 km) and VIIRS (375 m) counts are not on the same scale; compare them only through the MODIS-equivalent series.
Archives are clipped to the country by NASA; cells on the border only count the country's part.
Near-real-time months are provisional and lack the static-source flag, so a few industrial hotspots may remain.
No correction for satellite passes, clouds or viewing geometry.
